results.question: Which certifications must be retested if the PSM-28 module changes?
results.answer:
A change to the PSM-28 module requires re-testing under two records:

**1. TP-PSM-07 (power stage thermal and load qualification)** — required for any change to the regulator, inductor, or output capacitors on PSM-28, and for any new regulator candidate. Its three steps are:
- Full-load thermal soak at 70°C ambient in a sealed enclosure (TR-112, TP-PSM-07)
- Cold-start test at -20°C with firmware power sequencing enabled (added by Satish so any regulator change also re-checks power sequencing; slack #fw-team 2026-09-15)
- Load-step response and ripple check (TP-PSM-07)

**2. FW-233 / FW-PMIC-SEQ (power-good timing review)** — any regulator change on PSM-28 needs a firmware review of the power-good delay, otherwise the VX7 MCU can brown out during cold start (FW-233). Sai budgets a week of firmware work per candidate (PDU-48 kickoff).

Citations: TP-PSM-07, TR-112, FW-233, FW-PMIC-SEQ, HW-311.

results.question: According to the records, why does BCU-24 telemetry drop after a cold start?
results.answer: According to ticket SUP-1057, the BCU-24 Rev A loses CAN telemetry after a cold start because the CT-1051 CAN transceiver enters bus-off mode during the cold-start inrush, and the firmware never requests bus-off recovery — so telemetry stays down until someone power-cycles the charger. (Evidence: SUP-1057 comment by Nagarjun, 2026-10-14.)
